```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
data.table::setDTthreads(1L)
options(scipen = 999)
```

This article sets out the notation used in the other articles, which follows Leventer (2025), [*Identification of Child Penalties*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07486), and maps it to the output of the package.

## 1. The 2x2 comparison

The data have one row per person and age, with earnings $Y$, gender $G \in \{f, m\}$ and age at first birth $D$ ($D = \infty$ for a person who never has a child). A 2x2 comparison is indexed by:

| symbol | meaning | in the package |
|---|---|---|
| $g$ | gender, $f$ or $m$ | `female` |
| $d$ | treatment group: first birth at age $d$ | `d` |
| $a$ | target age | `a` |
| $d'$ | control group: first birth at age $d' > a$, not yet treated at the target age | `dp` |
| $d - 1$ | baseline age | `pre` (baseline $d - \text{pre}$) |
| $e = a - d$ | event time | `event_time` |
| $d' - d$ | control offset | `control_offset` |
| $D_{\max}$ | largest age at first birth used as a control group | `max_control_group` |

`multiple_treatment_group_analysis()` uses the closest not-yet-treated group as control group, $d' = a + 1$ (Section 1.3), so after treatment the control offset is $e + 1$. For $d = 26$:

| event time $e$ | target age $a$ | control group $d'$ | control offset $d' - d$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 26 | 27 | 1 |
| 1 | 27 | 28 | 2 |
| 2 | 28 | 29 | 3 |

## 2. Potential outcomes and causal estimands

$Y_a(d')$ is earnings at age $a$ had the first birth been at age $d'$, and $Y_a(\infty)$ earnings had there been no child; observed earnings are $Y_a = Y_a(D)$. Mean observed earnings of gender $g$ and treatment group $k$ at age $t$ are $\mu(g, k, t) = \mathbb{E}[Y_t \mid G = g, D = k]$. The average potential outcome (APO) is
$$
\mathrm{APO}(g, d, d', a) = \mathbb{E}\big[Y_a(d') \mid G = g,\, D = d\big],
$$
mean earnings at age $a$ of gender $g$ and treatment group $d$, had the first birth been at age $d'$. For a single $(d, a)$ the paper writes $\mathrm{APO}(g, d) \equiv \mathrm{APO}(g, d, d, a)$, which equals $\mu(g, d, a)$, and $\mathrm{APO}(g, \infty) \equiv \mathrm{APO}(g, d, \infty, a)$, mean earnings absent children. The causal estimands are (Sections 1.3 and 4.1):

| symbol | definition | in words |
|---|---|---|
| $\mathrm{ATE}(g)$ | $\mathrm{APO}(g, d) - \mathrm{APO}(g, \infty)$ | effect of parenthood on earnings |
| $\theta(g)$ | $\mathrm{ATE}(g) / \mathrm{APO}(g, \infty)$ | effect relative to earnings absent children |
| $\theta(f) - \theta(m)$ | | gender gap in normalized effects, the target of normalized event studies |
| $\rho(d')$ | $\mathrm{APO}(f, d, d', a) / \mathrm{APO}(m, d, d', a)$ | gender earnings ratio; $\rho(d)$ realized, $\rho(\infty)$ absent children |
| $\rho(d) - \rho(\infty)$ | | effect of parenthood on the gender earnings ratio |

In $\mathrm{APO}(g, d, d', a)$ and $\rho(d')$ the argument $d'$ is a counterfactual age at first birth, as in the paper; elsewhere $d'$ is the control group.

## 3. Output

`single_treatment_group_analysis()` returns one row per `method` and `estimand` for a cell $(d, d', a)$, and `multiple_treatment_group_analysis()` stacks these rows over cells. The columns are the cell (`d`, `dp`, `a`, `event_time`, `control_offset`), the row label (`method`, `estimand`), the estimate and its inference (`est`, `se`, `ci_l`, `ci_h`, `t`, `p`), and the number of persons by gender in the treatment and control group (`n_female_treat`, `n_female_control`, `n_male_treat`, `n_male_control`). Gaps are female minus male.

| `method` | `estimand` | the estimate | causal estimand it targets |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DID_Female`, `DID_Male` | `APO` | DID-imputed counterfactual earnings | $\mathrm{APO}(g, \infty)$ |
| `DID_Female`, `DID_Male` | `ATE` | DID | $\mathrm{ATE}(g)$ |
| `DID_Female`, `DID_Male` | `theta` | normalized DID | $\theta(g)$ |
| `TD` | `gap_ATE` | gender gap in DID | $\mathrm{ATE}(f) - \mathrm{ATE}(m)$ |
| `Conventional` | `gap_theta` | gender gap in normalized DID (the conventional estimator) | $\theta(f) - \theta(m)$ |
| `NTD` | `rho_effect` | observed minus DID-imputed gender earnings ratio (the new estimator) | $\rho(d) - \rho(\infty)$ |
| `NTD` | `rho_obs` | observed gender earnings ratio | $\rho(d)$ |
| `NTD` | `rho_cf` | gender ratio of DID-imputed counterfactual earnings | $\rho(\infty)$ |
| `NTD` | `share_parenthood` | parenthood's share of the observed gender gap | $[\rho(\infty) - \rho(d)] / [1 - \rho(d)]$ |
| `NTD` | `share_other` | the share of other factors | $[1 - \rho(\infty)] / [1 - \rho(d)]$ |
| `TD_E_LOGS` | `rho_effect`, `rho_obs`, `rho_cf`, `share_parenthood`, `share_other` | as `NTD`, with counterfactual earnings imputed multiplicatively | as `NTD` |
| `TD_PR` | `gap_theta_pre` | gender gap in effects relative to baseline earnings, imputed multiplicatively | $\dfrac{\mathrm{ATE}(f)}{\mathrm{APO}(f, d, \infty, d - 1)} - \dfrac{\mathrm{ATE}(m)}{\mathrm{APO}(m, d, \infty, d - 1)}$ |

The estimators, their standard errors, and the assumption under which each row identifies its target (with the result in the paper) are in [Estimation](estimators.html). `aggregate_estimands()` returns the same labels averaged over treatment groups ([Aggregation](aggregation.html)).

A cell of simulated data, treatment group $d = 26$ one year after the first birth ($a = 27$, $e = 1$) against the control group $d' = 28$:

```{r example}
library(childpen)
sim <- simulate_data(2000, 24:30)
res <- single_treatment_group_analysis(sim, d = 26, dp = 28, a = 27)
res[1, c("d", "dp", "a", "event_time", "control_offset")]
shown <- res[res$method %in% c("DID_Female", "Conventional", "NTD"),
             c("method", "estimand", "est", "se", "ci_l", "ci_h")]
shown[3:6] <- round(shown[3:6], 3)
shown
```
